sources.claim: The ticket reports new installs fail with ModuleNotFoundError for mcp.server.fastmcp because the mcp SDK 2.0 moved that module.
FR-001 requires the mcp cli dependency to carry an upper bound excluding mcp 2.0.0 and later.
FR-002 requires a fresh resolution to select mcp on the 1.x line and never 2.x.
FR-003 requires all existing mcp.server.fastmcp imports to keep working with no migration to 2.0 paths.
FR-005 requires an automated regression guard test that fails on a non-1 mcp major version or a broken import surface.
FR-004 requires no runtime logic, handler, API-client, config, or interface change; only the dependency specifier changes.
Design alternatives select Option A, the upper-bound cap, over exact-pin and mcp 2.0 migration.
The plan Pin change section specifies changing the pyproject dependency to the upper-bounded form as the selected option A.
The plan Regression guard section specifies the version and import-surface guard tests.
Runtime Data Availability Proof shows no runtime data is read or written; the mcp import resolves at install time.
T004 applies the pin cap in pyproject line 20.
T002 and T003 add the version-major and import-surface guard tests.
T007 verifies the production diff is limited to the pin, the new test file, and optionally uv.lock.
test-scenarios maps the version-cap and import-surface guard scenarios to the requirements.
The Constitution Check section evaluates all five principles as PASS with no violations.
main.py imports FastMCP from mcp.server.fastmcp, the import surface that must keep working.
Scenario S4 verifies no production behavior change by running the full existing suite unchanged.
The Assumption Ledger records A1/A2 (mcp 1.x exports fastmcp; 2.0 moved it), proven by the ticket traceback, and the cap validated by resolution and import tests.
